text:
incident-bot: Pager — SEV2: spike in SRV lookup timeouts for internal service 'api-backend' in us-west-2a. Alerts: 85% of CoreDNS queries returning SERVFAIL or timing out, automatic retries causing backend 502s for some customers. Runbook: /runbooks/dns-service-failures (link)
alice-sre: acked. I'm on it, pulling logs from coredns in us-west-2a.
alice-sre: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep coredns
alice-sre: coredns-0  CrashLoopBackOff  1/1  10.0.12.45  us-west-2a
alice-sre: coredns-1  Running          1/1  10.0.23.17  us-west-2b
alice-sre: grabbing coredns logs from the CrashLoopBackOff pod
alice-sre: ```
2026-03-15T14:52:02.123Z [ERROR] plugin/forward: failed to forward query: dial udp 10.0.0.2:53: i/o timeout
2026-03-15T14:52:02.124Z [WARN] can't reach upstream: 10.0.0.2
```
sanjay-netops: @alice-sre seeing similar telemetry from VPC flow logs — big packet drops for 10.0.12.0/24 in us-west-2a across multiple hosts. AWS support ticket open, fabric errors in AZ reported. link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#caseId=12345
maria-prodeng: quick customer impact: logs show ~8% of requests to customer-facing ingress in us-west-2a returning 502s over the last 8 minutes. Global traffic is fine; this is a partial AZ-level impact.
alice-sre: repro steps: dig SRV _api._tcp.svc.cluster.local @10.0.12.45
alice-sre: ```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> _api._tcp.svc.cluster.local @10.0.12.45
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
leah-support: field reports from a large customer in us-west show intermittent 502 spikes starting ~14:45 UTC, escalated to AE.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-022. Sev2. Pager: alice-sre, sara-oncall.
alice-sre: mitigation plan I'm trying now:
- cordon + drain the affected coredns node to move coredns pod to healthy AZ
- scale coredns replicas to 4 to increase redundancy
- update service-discovery fallback policy to prefer us-west-2b/c
alice-sre: rolling restart of coredns-0
alice-sre: ```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns
# waiting for pods
```
sanjay-netops: AWS confirmed degraded fabric in us-west-2a; they're recommending shifting critical control plane components out of the AZ until they fix it. ETA unknown.
maria-prodeng: can we patch routing at the service mesh level to avoid nodes in us-west-2a? We should mitigate impact to customers by steering away from that AZ.
alice-sre: increasing coredns replicas to 4 and adding anti-affinity so they land outside the failed node pool.
alice-sre: ```
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment coredns --replicas=4
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep coredns
```
alice-sre: new coredns pods spawned in us-west-2b and us-west-2c. The CrashLoopBackOff instance stayed terminated.
sanjay-netops: I've applied a temporary route update on the internal load balancer to reduce traffic to instances in us-west-2a for service discovery endpoints.
maria-prodeng: traffic metrics look better — 502 rate down from 8% to 1.2% over the last 5 minutes. Still seeing occasional errors for long-tail sessions.
leah-support: notifying affected customers with a brief status update. Template: "We are investigating increased errors in us-west-2a impacting some API calls. Working on mitigation; no action required from customers." :email:
alice-sre: digging into consul/etcd side of service discovery — Consul metrics show higher RPC latency from agents in us-west-2a to servers.
alice-sre: consul operator check
alice-sre: ```
consul operator raft list-peers
# peers show one follower with high RTT (us-west-2a)
```
sanjay-netops: AWS says they've applied a partial fix and are seeing packet loss drop. They want us to keep traffic diverted for 15 minutes then gradually restore.
maria-prodeng: recommend we keep coredns scaled and anti-affinity for the rest of the day and run an eval of DNS TTLs and caches. Also run post-incident eval for routing fallbacks.
alice-sre: I'm going to keep monitoring for 30m. If errors stay below 1% we'll reduce priority. Adding short term follow-ups:
- validate all CoreDNS pods stable in us-west-2b/c
- verify Consul raft health and leader stability
- run synthetic SRV queries from multiple AZs
sara-oncall: taking over on-call at 15:03 UTC. Summary: SEV2 due to AZ-level networking degradation in us-west-2a causing CoreDNS/Consul RPC timeouts and SRV lookup failures. Mitigations applied: scaled and redistributed CoreDNS, ILB steering away from us-west-2a, AWS ticket open. Current impact: degraded but largely mitigated — ~1% request errors remaining.
sara-oncall: handoff notes: continue monitoring error budget and customer escalations. If error >3% for 5 minutes escalate to SEV1 and re-pager.
leah-support: confirmed customers in us-west notified; AE escalation opened for 2 customers with SLO impacts.
incident-bot: Handoff acknowledged. On-call owner: sara-oncall. Incident INC-2026-03-15-022 is active. Next update expected in 30 minutes or on any regression.
sara-oncall: closing loop: will file a postmortem with timeline, root cause analysis (AWS AZ fabric + insufficient multi-AZ placement for control-plane DNS), and remediation: stricter anti-affinity for coredns, lower DNS TTLs for critical services, automated ILB failover playbook. ETA PM: tomorrow 18:00 PST.
alice-sre: thanks team. I'll add the logs and dig outputs to the incident ticket for the postmortem. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-03-15-022 annotated: mitigations applied, handoff complete.
